Declan Rice and Kobbie Mainoo formed the defensive pivot initially, with Phil Foden operating as a left winger and Jude Bellingham as a left-sided attacking presence, allowing Bukayo Saka to function on the right wing. Following Mainoo's substitution for Cole Palmer at 69 minutes, England repositioned into a less rigid setup; Bellingham shifted to a right defensive midfield role (template position 40.0, 62.0), and Foden moved to the left wing, freeing Palmer to act as attacking midfielder. By the 89th minute, England had formally declared a 4-1-2-1-2 formation, centralizing Rice as a lone defensive midfielder (template 40.0, 40.0) with Bellingham and Saka redeployed as central midfielders flanking Palmer in the number ten slot, whilst Ivan Toney and Watkins formed a two-striker pairing.

The wider attacking players—Nico Williams (78.1, 30.4) and Lamine Yamal (81.1, 68.6)—advanced significantly into the attacking third. As the match progressed through substitutions and fatigue, this shape fractured; by the 82–88 minute window, Carvajal had drifted even further upfield (108.0, 62.6), indicative of Spain's attacking intent in the latter stages. England's on-ball positioning showed a more compact midfield structure. From there the ball went wide rather than through the middle — Carvajal→Yamal nine times, Laporte→Cucurella nine, Cucurella→Nico Williams seven — while Olmo (11 passes) and Morata (8) were the least-involved outfielders in the network, a front pairing served rather than used as a relay.
